title: Field service & inspection
tagline: A technician photographs equipment and gets an instant assessment — what it is, what looks wrong, what to do next. No connectivity required, so it works in the truck, the plant, or the basement.
scenario: A junior tech is in front of a switch cabinet they've never seen. They snap a photo, and the AI identifies the hardware, flags the frayed cable and blocked vents, and suggests the checks a senior tech would run — expertise on tap, on site, offline.
steps: The button below opens Vision with an inspection prompt ready to go.
Drop in any photo — equipment, a server rack, even a picture from your phone.
For full effect: turn off Wi-Fi first and show that nothing changes.

ctas.label: Run it live in Vision →
ctas.prompt: You are assisting a field service technician. Identify the equipment in this photo, note any visible damage, wear, or safety concerns, and recommend next steps.

why.head: Works offline
why.body: job sites, secure facilities, and vehicles rarely have reliable uplink.

why.head: Photos stay local
why.body: site imagery often can't legally leave the premises.

notes: Keep two or three good equipment photos in a folder on the desktop so this demo never depends on finding one live.
The offline angle lands hardest with manufacturing, utilities, and public-sector audiences.
